https://www.belfastlive.co.uk/news/uk-wo.text: The south's Foreign Affairs Minister Helen McEntee has praised members of the Dublin Civil Defence for coming to the aid of those injured in a mass shooting in Poland. Six people were shot dead , and 15 were injured when a gunman opened fire in Krakow's main square in the Old Town at around 3pm Irish time on Saturday. The Fine Gael deputy said the incident was a "truly devastating attack on innocent civilians who were going about their daily lives". Polish Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz declared the attack an "act of terror". Members of the Dublin Civil Defence were in Krakow for a holiday when the incident took place. Civil Defence Officer James McConnell said he and fellow members ran to help the injured people by performing CPR and stemming the bleeding. Ms McEntee said: "I think it is extraordinary the way in which, I suppose, the values and the work that they engage in at home went straight into action in Kraków. "They were there to support very vulnerable people who had been involved in that attack and to assist them. And so, obviously, I just want to thank them publicly. "(I'm) very glad that they're okay and they're safe, but (I'm) very conscious that there were a lot of innocent civilians caught up in this, and (it's) obviously a very scary scenario for everybody." It comes as three other bodies were found at the suspect's home, and were later identified as the man's parents and sister. In response to queries, the Department of Foreign Affairs said they're not aware of any Irish citizens directly affected. But a spokesperson said they are providing "consular assistance to a small number of Irish citizens". In a statement, they said: "The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade is aware of the serious incident in Krakow, Poland and is monitoring the situation closely. "The Department is not aware of any Irish citizens directly affected. "However, the Embassy of Ireland in Poland is providing consular assistance to a small number of Irish citizens who have sought advice and guidance following the incident."
